I think we should move this hook to the PostgreSQL's introspection e.g. `is_table(table_name)`:
```python
def is_table(self, table_name):
    with self.connection.cursor() as cursor:
        cursor.execute("""
            SELECT TRUE
            FROM pg_class c
            JOIN pg_namespace n ON c.relnamespace = n.oid
            WHERE
               c.relname = %s AND
               c.relkind = 'r' AND
               n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'pg_toast') AND
               pg_catalog.pg_table_is_visible(c.oid)
       """, [model._meta.db_table])
       return cursor.fetchone() is not None
```
~Also this should be cached e.g. `lru_cache(maxsize=512)` we don't want to perform an extra query each time.~

body:
I think this sentence isn't enough. 

* You have to override the method on the features class, 
* Then, override the database wrapper, 
* Then, save it in the right place, i.e. a `my_backend.base`, pointing `DATABASES` (`BACKEND`) to `my_backend`. (This last one is not obvious at all I think.)

I think we need an example of that. 

So here, broken up for consideration: 

```
The new ``allows_group_by_selected_pks_on_model()`` method of
``django.db.backends.base.BaseDatabaseFeatures`` allows optimization of ``GROUP
BY`` clauses to require only the selected models' primary keys.

This optimization is currently only supported on PostgreSQL. By default,
it is only applied to **managed models**.

To enable the the GROUP BY primary key-only optimization for unmanaged models,
subclass the PostgreSQL database engine, overriding the features class
``allows_group_by_selected_pks_on_model()`` as you require. See LINK TO FULL
EXAMPLE for an example.
```

Then in FULL EXAMPLE we need the full example @Tasssadar came up with [in this comment](https://github.com/django/django/pull/11606#issuecomment-517255305), plus the file to save it in, and the `DATABASES` setting example. 

Open to suggestions as to where but I would create a new section in `databases.txt` called, `Subclassing the built-in backends`, just before `Using a 3rd-party database backend`, to hold FULL EXAMPLE (and be the target of LINK TO FULL EXAMPLE).
